1_Learning_Objective.Title: 🎯 The "Why Are We Learning This?" (Learning Objective)
1_Learning_Objective.Content: The core takeaway is to help your child identify basic body parts (hands, legs, eyes, head) and confidently connect them to simple action words (clap, tap, open, side-to-side). It builds foundational vocabulary, rhythm, and body awareness!

2_The_Hook.Title: 🪝 The Hook (How to start the conversation)
2_The_Hook.Content: While sitting at the dining table or walking around the house, casually ask: **'Hey, can you make a sound using just your body, without opening your mouth?'** (Let them experiment until they clap or stomp). Then smile and say: **'Wow! Our bodies are like little musical instruments. Let's see what else they can do in our new chapter!'**

Mini_Lessons.What_To_Say: Tell your child: 'Look at your hands. We have one, two little hands. What happens when we bring them together quickly? They go clap, clap, clap!'
Mini_Lessons.Home_Example: Play a quick high-five game. Ask them to give you a 'slow five' and then a 'fast clap'. Clap along to the beat of their favorite cartoon song.

Mini_Lessons.What_To_Say: Tell your child: 'Now look down. We have two little legs. What sound do our feet make on the floor? Let's make our toes go tap, tap, tap!'
Mini_Lessons.Home_Example: Sit together on the floor. First, tap your fingers on the ground, then show them how to gently 'tap' their feet on the floor like little raindrops.

Mini_Lessons.What_To_Say: Tell your child: 'How do you look at a big airplane in the sky? Your two little eyes open wide! And how do you say no without talking? Your one little head goes side to side!'
Mini_Lessons.Home_Example: Play 'Peek-a-boo' but exaggerate opening your eyes wide. Then ask them a silly question like, 'Do dogs fly?' so they have to shake their head side-to-side.

4_Common_Stumbling_Blocks.Title: 🚧 Common Stumbling Blocks (What to watch out for)
4_Common_Stumbling_Blocks.Content:
At this age, kids often confuse **'tapping'** with **'stomping'**. 
*   **How to clarify:** Show them the difference! Stomping uses the whole foot and is loud (like an elephant). Tapping uses just the toes and is quiet (like a mouse). This helps them learn fine motor control and nuance in words.

Questions.Question: What do our two little hands do in the poem?
If I want to look at a giant balloon, what do my eyes do?
We have two hands and two legs. But how many heads do we have to shake side-to-side?

Activities.Name: 1. The Musical Body (Simon Says)
Activities.Description: Play a mini version of 'Simon Says'. Say: 'Simon says... make your hands go clap, clap!' or 'Simon says... make your head go side to side!' Mix it up to make it silly.

Activities.Name: 2. Shadow Hands
Activities.Description: Turn off the lights and use a phone flashlight against a blank wall. Make shadow hands and 'clap' them together, then have your child try to make their shadow legs 'tap'.

Activities.Name: 3. The Slow-Mo Action Game
Activities.Description: Call out an action like 'Clap' or 'Tap' and hold up a turtle toy (do it in super slow motion) or a racecar toy (do it super fast!).
